text:
A young painter spent six months working on a portrait. When it was finished, he put it in the town square and wrote a sign next to it: “Please mark every mistake with a red cross.”

By the evening, the painting was covered in red crosses. The painter felt terrible and went home in tears.

His teacher visited him that night. “Why are you crying?” he asked.

“Everybody hated my painting,” said the young man. “Look how many mistakes they found!”

The teacher thought for a moment. “Tomorrow, make another copy of the painting,” he said. “This time, write a different sign: ‘Please mark the parts you like with a green circle.’”

The painter did as he was told. By the end of the next day, the second painting was covered in green circles. Many people had marked exactly the same parts that others had crossed out the day before.

The painter was confused. “I don’t understand,” he said.

“You can’t please everyone,” said the teacher. “Every person sees something different. Listen to the advice you can learn from, but don’t let it destroy your confidence.”

The painter smiled for the first time in two days.

Moral: Opinions are different, so don’t let criticism stop you.

quiz.q: The painter worked on the portrait for six months.
What did the second sign ask people to do?
o: Mark the parts they like with a green circle
Mark every mistake with a red cross

quiz.q: What was surprising about the green circles?
o: People liked the same parts others had crossed out

quiz.q: Opinions are different, so don't let ___ stop you.
